subject.title: [Bug]: When an embedded agent attempt triggers overflow-recovery auto-compaction, the compaction path re-acquires the same session's write lock inside the same process

question: Should maintainers land the narrow direct-compaction reentry fix now, or wait for the broader inner-writer lock policy work?
rationale: The issue is source-reproducible, but reentrant session locks are a session-state boundary, and the open PRs differ in scope and proof quality.

options.title: Land Narrow Compaction Fix
options.body: Accept direct compaction as the same logical writer and land https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/88919 or an equivalent focused patch first.

options.title: Wait For Broader Inner-Writer Policy
options.body: Hold the issue for https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/96000 or an owner-led broader patch after proof and test blockers are resolved.

options.title: Split Follow-Up Work
options.body: Land the compaction fix now and open or keep a separate follow-up for tool-result truncation and transcript rewrite reentry.

recommendation.title: Land Narrow Compaction Fix
recommendation.body: Accept direct compaction as the same logical writer and land https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/88919 or an equivalent focused patch first.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent path history and area work make this the best available routing candidate for the session-state merge-risk choice.
